definitions.explanation: A price that is high relative to normal or expected levels. Commonly used in financial markets, shopping, and economic discussions. The opposite is {安値|やすね}.

examples.japanese: {株|かぶ}が{高値|たかね}をつけた。
{今年|ことし}の{最|さい}{高値|たかね}を{更新|こうしん}した。
examples.english: It set a new high for the year.

examples.japanese: {円安|えんやす}の{影響|えいきょう}で{輸入品|ゆにゅうひん}が{高値|たかね}で{取引|とりひき}されており、{消費者|しょうひしゃ}の{負担|ふたん}が{増|ふ}えている。
examples.english: Due to the weak yen, imported goods are trading at high prices, increasing the burden on consumers.

notes:
A compound of {高|たか} (high) + {値|ね} (price/value). Standard financial and commercial vocabulary.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {高値|たかね}をつける (reach a high price)
- {高値|たかね}を{更新|こうしん}する (set a new high)
- {最|さい}{高値|たかね} (highest price, all-time high)
- {高値|たかね}で{売|う}る (sell at a high price)
- {高値|たかね}{圏|けん} (high-price range)

SIMILAR WORDS:
The opposite is {安値|やすね} (low price). For general "expensive" in everyday speech, {高|たか}い is more natural. {高値|たかね} specifically refers to a price level, especially in market and trading contexts.
